criteria.title: VOCAL PERFORMANCE: Vocal Technique and Musical Accuracy
assessment_focus: Accurate pitch, secure harmonies, and rhythmic precision
Clear diction, breath support, and smooth vocal transitions
Consistent technique, unified tone, and intentional vocal shaping across soloists and ensemble
Purposeful phrasing and dynamics that support musical expression and the emotional arc

levels.label: Superior
levels.observable: Ensemble and leads demonstrate exceptional pitch accuracy, rhythmic control, sustained breath support, and crisp diction throughout. All relevant passages demonstrate pitch, rhythmic accuracy, and harmonies; breath support, diction, and smooth vocal transitions; and solo/ensemble consistency and expressive phrase shaping, without a consequential lapse.
levels.example: In a hypothetical high-school production of Dear Evan Hansen, the rapid, emotionally charged text of “Waving Through a Window” remains intelligible because the soloist maintains centered pitch, planned breaths, and crisp final consonants. When “You Will Be Found” expands from solo voice to overlapping ensemble harmony, entries align rhythmically, vowels match, and the increasing volume never distorts the pitches. The same assurance carries across exposed and full-company passages, so the technical work strengthens the emotional climax rather than drawing attention to itself.

levels.label: Excellent+
levels.observable: Strong control with only minor inconsistencies in pitch, timing, or breath. Diction is clear in nearly every moment. Nearly every passage demonstrates pitch, rhythmic accuracy, and harmonies as well as breath support, diction, and smooth vocal transitions; at most one isolated lapse in solo/ensemble consistency and expressive phrase shaping is quickly resolved.
levels.example: In “For Forever,” the singer maintains confident pitch and clear storytelling over almost the entire number, with securely supported long phrases. One transition is rushed as a breath comes later than planned, briefly unsettling the rhythm. The next line settles immediately back into tempo. In “Sincerely, Me,” an isolated change in vowel clarity slightly blurs a harmony, but ensemble tuning and diction remain dependable. These are uncommon, quickly recovered slips—not a recurring technical problem.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.observable: Solid technique overall, though phrasing or tone may occasionally falter. Most relevant passages demonstrate pitch, rhythmic accuracy, and harmonies; a few minor, separate lapses affect breath support, diction, and smooth vocal transitions or solo/ensemble consistency and expressive phrase shaping without forming a pattern.
levels.example: During “Only Us,” both singers sustain a connected duet with mostly clear lyrics and well-coordinated phrasing, but the tuning of one exposed final note briefly wavers. In “You Will Be Found,” the ensemble builds accurately and with evident preparation, although one supporting part grows too forceful and loses tonal unity for a phrase. Neither issue persists, and the audience can still follow the musical and emotional progression. The performance is reliably strong with several small, separate imperfections.

levels.label: Strong
levels.observable: Technique is evident but often compromised by unsupported tone or rhythmic inaccuracies. Many passages achieve pitch, rhythmic accuracy, and harmonies, but recurring problems with breath support, diction, and smooth vocal transitions or solo/ensemble consistency and expressive phrase shaping interrupt otherwise effective moments.
levels.example: In “Disappear,” the ensemble reaches several well-coordinated musical phrases, yet multiple group entrances begin tentatively instead of landing together. Breath support weakens on long sustained notes, causing some voices to sag in pitch, and excited passages rush ahead of the established pulse more than once. The audience understands the scene, but recurring execution problems interrupt the musical flow. This is more than the occasional isolated lapse expected of an 8.

levels.label: Good+
levels.observable: Frequent lapses in pitch or timing. Diction is unclear or dropped in several lines. Repeated attempts at pitch, rhythmic accuracy, and harmonies, together with breath support, diction, and smooth vocal transitions, are evident, yet solo/ensemble consistency and expressive phrase shaping succeeds only intermittently.
levels.example: The ensemble attacks “Good for You” with commitment, and parts of the chorus align rhythmically; however, consonants blur repeatedly when the texture thickens. During “Requiem,” a harmony briefly locks into tune but drifts again after several sustained notes. Breath and pitch corrections are audible from phrase to phrase. The singers consistently attempt the intended technique, yet they achieve reliable clarity only in some passages, making the storytelling uneven.

levels.label: Good
levels.observable: Several technical issues reduce clarity and storytelling impact. Some passages demonstrate pitch, rhythmic accuracy, and harmonies; inconsistent breath support, diction, and smooth vocal transitions and solo/ensemble consistency and expressive phrase shaping prevent those successes from carrying through the performance.
levels.example: In “Waving Through a Window,” occasional phrases have centered pitch and intelligible words, but several verses lose their consonants, and unplanned breaths divide thoughts mid-line. As the chorus arrives, the relationship between melody and supporting harmony changes unpredictably from one entrance to the next. The musical intention is recognizable in a few moments, yet the technical execution is not sustained long enough to carry the number convincingly.

levels.label: Developing
levels.observable: Technique is weak overall. Ensemble and leads struggle to maintain accuracy or breath control. Occasional efforts at pitch, rhythmic accuracy, and harmonies are evident, but repeated problems with breath support, diction, and smooth vocal transitions and solo/ensemble consistency and expressive phrase shaping obscure most relevant moments.
levels.example: In “Words Fail,” the performer finds the melody briefly at the start of a quiet phrase, but sustained notes repeatedly drift off pitch and dropped consonants obscure important words. The singer appears to restart breath support after the musical line has already begun, creating uneven phrasing. Even a supportive ensemble entrance does not consistently stabilize the number. Only occasional moments communicate the intended vocal technique; most of the passage remains insecure.

levels.label: Fair+
levels.observable: Multiple vocal challenges affect lyric comprehension and distract from the narrative. Only rare passages achieve pitch, rhythmic accuracy, and harmonies; persistent weaknesses in breath support, diction, and smooth vocal transitions and solo/ensemble consistency and expressive phrase shaping undermine the major moments.
levels.example: In “You Will Be Found,” the company communicates energy at the opening of the ensemble build, but harmony parts frequently separate in pitch and entrances no longer share a reliable pulse. “Sincerely, Me” contains a few recognizable, accurately sung lines, surrounded by repeated rhythmic disagreement and unclear diction. The audience can identify the songs but struggles to understand the lyrics or hear the intended harmonic arrival. Effective musical execution is rare.

levels.label: Fair
levels.observable: Major issues in pitch, timing, and diction across multiple songs. Convincing pitch, rhythmic accuracy, and harmonies is barely present, while substantial failures in breath support, diction, and smooth vocal transitions and solo/ensemble consistency and expressive phrase shaping dominate the performance.
levels.example: In a hypothetical “Anybody Have a Map?” performance, nearly every overlapping entrance begins at a different moment, so the conversation-like musical exchange loses its rhythmic shape. Ensemble harmony breaks apart across sustained notes, and most lyrics become unintelligible as singers search for pitches and breaths. A rare short phrase lands together, but the correction does not carry into the next section. The technical gaps dominate what the audience hears.

levels.label: Inadequate
levels.observable: Persistent vocal problems render music ineffective. Across relevant moments, pitch, rhythmic accuracy, and harmonies; breath support, diction, and smooth vocal transitions; and solo/ensemble consistency and expressive phrase shaping are virtually absent or ineffective.
levels.example: In a hypothetical “You Will Be Found,” the ensemble repeatedly begins after or before the musical cues, with little shared pitch center and almost no intelligible text. Even the climactic unison idea cannot be heard as a coordinated musical statement: breath support collapses, harmony parts never settle, and rhythmic agreement is virtually absent. Rather than reinforcing the story’s collective emotional release, the vocal execution prevents the central musical moment from being communicated.

criteria.title: STYLISTIC CHOICES: Lyric Interpretation and Emotional Storytelling
assessment_focus: Purposeful phrasing, dynamics, inflection, and vocal tone
Nuanced, authentic lyric interpretation that communicates character, intention, and emotion
Character-driven vocal choices that advance the narrative for soloists and ensemble
Consistent, character-appropriate vocal styles, accents, and dialects when relevant

levels.label: Superior
levels.observable: Musical phrasing and expression enhanced character and plot; emotional arcs are deeply felt and clearly shaped through vocal performance. Nuanced, character-appropriate vocal styles are sustained when relevant. All relevant passages demonstrate lyric intention and emotional inflection; nuanced phrasing, dynamics, and appropriate vocal styles; and character-specific storytelling by soloists and ensemble, without a consequential lapse.
levels.example: In Dear Evan Hansen, “Words Fail” builds dynamically from introspective to cathartic. “You Will Be Found” crescendos with layered meaning and connection. Each phrase supports the character’s emotional state with precise dynamics and clarity. At an emotionally exposed sung confession, vocal inflection, vowel color, and dynamics reveal the character’s changing intention. This clarity holds through exposed details as well as the busiest parts of the sequence; the audience receives the dramatic information without having to compensate for performance or design problems.

levels.label: Excellent+
levels.observable: Emotionally compelling and well-phrased, with a few missed interpretive nuances. Nearly every passage demonstrates lyric intention and emotional inflection as well as nuanced phrasing, dynamics, and appropriate vocal styles; at most one isolated lapse in character-specific storytelling by soloists and ensemble is quickly resolved.
levels.example: “For Forever” has a strong emotional shape but slightly flattens in the bridge. A few transitions in “Only Us” could have used more vocal contrast to heighten intimacy. At an emotionally exposed sung confession, vocal inflection, vowel color, and dynamics reveal the character’s changing intention for nearly the entire sequence. On one brief occasion, phrases stay uniformly loud or use a style at odds with the character’s state; the issue is corrected immediately, so the intended storytelling remains clear. That isolated lapse distinguishes this from completely sustained excellence.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.observable: Storytelling is mostly successful with expressive tone and intention, but interpretation could be deeper or more consistent. Most relevant passages demonstrate lyric intention and emotional inflection; a few minor, separate lapses affect nuanced phrasing, dynamics, and appropriate vocal styles or character-specific storytelling by soloists and ensemble without forming a pattern.
levels.example: “Requiem” is sung with appropriate tone, but subtle differences in phrasing or dynamic level could better highlight Zoe’s emotional conflict. At an emotionally exposed sung confession, vocal inflection, vowel color, and dynamics reveal the character’s changing intention in most moments. A few separate beats reveal that phrases stay uniformly loud or use a style at odds with the character’s state, but they are small and do not develop into a recurring weakness. The audience can still understand the scene’s central intention.

levels.label: Strong
levels.observable: Moments of emotional storytelling are present, but phrasing or intensity often lack clarity or purpose. Expressive inflection or vocal style is uneven in several moments. Many passages achieve lyric intention and emotional inflection, but recurring problems with nuanced phrasing, dynamics, and appropriate vocal styles or character-specific storytelling by soloists and ensemble interrupt otherwise effective moments.
levels.example: In “If I Could Tell Her,” the performer captures nervous energy but doesn’t build the scene’s emotional arc vocally. At an emotionally exposed sung confession, there are effective stretches in which vocal inflection, vowel color, and dynamics reveal the character’s changing intention. However, phrases stay uniformly loud or use a style at odds with the character’s state at several points. Because the problem recurs rather than appearing once, the audience hears the melody but misses the emotional turn during parts of the sequence, even though the overall scene still communicates.

levels.label: Good+
levels.observable: Expression is generalized; phrasing lacks shape or emotional purpose. Repeated attempts at lyric intention and emotional inflection, together with nuanced phrasing, dynamics, and appropriate vocal styles, are evident, yet character-specific storytelling by soloists and ensemble succeeds only intermittently.
levels.example: “Waving Through a Window” is technically clean but sung at a single dynamic level, reducing its vulnerability and urgency. At an emotionally exposed sung confession, some passages succeed because vocal inflection, vowel color, and dynamics reveal the character’s changing intention. However, phrases stay uniformly loud or use a style at odds with the character’s state in many of the more demanding moments. The intended effect is attempted throughout, but the audience hears the melody but misses the emotional turn often enough that the result is only intermittently secure.

levels.label: Good
levels.observable: Interpretation is inconsistent or disconnected; lyrics feel recited, not felt. Some passages demonstrate lyric intention and emotional inflection; inconsistent nuanced phrasing, dynamics, and appropriate vocal styles and character-specific storytelling by soloists and ensemble prevent those successes from carrying through the performance.
levels.example: “To Break in a Glove” lacks emotional depth; intention behind lines is unclear. “Good for You” is sung with strong volume but limited inflection. At an emotionally exposed sung confession, a few isolated moments show that vocal inflection, vowel color, and dynamics reveal the character’s changing intention. Elsewhere, phrases stay uniformly loud or use a style at odds with the character’s state frequently; as a result, the audience hears the melody but misses the emotional turn and the dramatic intention comes through only in patches. The successes are real, but they do not yet form a dependable pattern.

levels.label: Developing
levels.observable: Limited emotional connection; musical storytelling fails to support character journey. Lyrics and character-specific inflection often fail to connect. Occasional efforts at lyric intention and emotional inflection are evident, but repeated problems with nuanced phrasing, dynamics, and appropriate vocal styles and character-specific storytelling by soloists and ensemble obscure most relevant moments.
levels.example: “Requiem” feels rushed and vocally tense, obscuring the meaning behind the family’s grief. At an emotionally exposed sung confession, one brief passage suggests that vocal inflection, vowel color, and dynamics reveal the character’s changing intention. In most passages, however, phrases stay uniformly loud or use a style at odds with the character’s state. Consequently, the audience hears the melody but misses the emotional turn; the results are mixed and the dramatic intention is only occasionally recognizable.

levels.label: Fair+
levels.observable: Emotionally flat or overacted phrasing undermines the lyric’s meaning. Only rare passages achieve lyric intention and emotional inflection; persistent weaknesses in nuanced phrasing, dynamics, and appropriate vocal styles and character-specific storytelling by soloists and ensemble undermine the major moments.
levels.example: “Words Fail” lacks emotional pacing—either rushed or overly dramatic without believable transition. At an emotionally exposed sung confession, only a few fragments suggest that vocal inflection, vowel color, and dynamics reveal the character’s changing intention. Much more often, phrases stay uniformly loud or use a style at odds with the character’s state; the audience hears the melody but misses the emotional turn across the number. The audience might recognize one successful beat but cannot rely on the criterion being achieved.

levels.label: Fair
levels.observable: No evident connection to text or character; line delivery is mechanical. Convincing lyric intention and emotional inflection is barely present, while substantial failures in nuanced phrasing, dynamics, and appropriate vocal styles and character-specific storytelling by soloists and ensemble dominate the performance.
levels.example: “Only Us” is sung with little variation or interaction between performers. Emotion feels forced or absent. At an emotionally exposed sung confession, a rare moment hints that vocal inflection, vowel color, and dynamics reveal the character’s changing intention, but phrases stay uniformly loud or use a style at odds with the character’s state dominates almost every relevant passage. Consequently, the audience hears the melody but misses the emotional turn to such an extent that the principal musical or dramatic information is obscured.

levels.label: Inadequate
levels.observable: Performance lacks any emotional relevance or vocal expression. Across relevant moments, lyric intention and emotional inflection; nuanced phrasing, dynamics, and appropriate vocal styles; and character-specific storytelling by soloists and ensemble are virtually absent or ineffective.
levels.example: In “Words Fail,” the words are delivered without shaped phrasing, dynamic change, or evident connection to Evan’s emotional turning point. At an emotionally exposed sung confession, there is virtually no sustained moment in which vocal inflection, vowel color, and dynamics reveal the character’s changing intention. Instead, phrases stay uniformly loud or use a style at odds with the character’s state throughout the sequence; the audience hears the melody but misses the emotional turn so consistently that the intended contribution to the production is nearly absent.

criteria.title: BALANCE AND BLEND: Soloists, Ensemble, Vocal Parts, and Accompaniment
assessment_focus: Balanced soloist and ensemble sound; clear blend among harmonized vocal parts
Individual voices and sections heard without unintentionally overpowering others
Appropriate musical balance between singers and live or recorded accompaniment
Dynamic sensitivity and unified blend that support clarity and storytelling

levels.label: Superior
levels.observable: Ensemble and soloists maintain excellent balance across vocal sections and with instrumental backing. Every voice part supports the whole without overpowering. Harmonized vocal parts blend cleanly without masking each other. All relevant passages demonstrate balance between soloists and ensemble; blend among harmonized vocal parts; and sensitivity between voices and live or recorded accompaniment, without a consequential lapse.
levels.example: In Dear Evan Hansen, “You Will Be Found” builds from solo to full ensemble with seamless blend. All voice parts—especially alto/tenor harmonies—are present without drowning out the lead or track. At a passage where solo voices and harmonies overlap, the lead line remains distinct while supporting parts blend rather than compete. This clarity holds through exposed details as well as the busiest parts of the sequence; the audience receives the dramatic information without having to compensate for performance or design problems.

levels.label: Excellent+
levels.observable: Strong ensemble and solo blend with only brief moments of imbalance. Nearly every passage demonstrates balance between soloists and ensemble as well as blend among harmonized vocal parts; at most one isolated lapse in sensitivity between voices and live or recorded accompaniment is quickly resolved.
levels.example: “Sincerely, Me” has well-balanced group vocals, though occasional emphasis on one harmony line disrupts blend. At a passage where solo voices and harmonies overlap, the lead line remains distinct while supporting parts blend rather than compete for nearly the entire sequence. On one brief occasion, one part dominates the texture or the accompanying sound masks the lead; the issue is corrected immediately, so the intended storytelling remains clear. That isolated lapse distinguishes this from completely sustained excellence.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.observable: General vocal blend is solid, though solo or group parts occasionally dominate or disappear. Most relevant passages demonstrate balance between soloists and ensemble; a few minor, separate lapses affect blend among harmonized vocal parts or sensitivity between voices and live or recorded accompaniment without forming a pattern.
levels.example: In “Requiem,” the mezzo line overpowers other harmonies briefly. Instrumental backing slightly overpowers vocals at the climax. At a passage where solo voices and harmonies overlap, the lead line remains distinct while supporting parts blend rather than compete in most moments. A few separate beats reveal that one part dominates the texture or the accompanying sound masks the lead, but they are small and do not develop into a recurring weakness. The audience can still understand the scene’s central intention.

levels.label: Strong
levels.observable: Balance is inconsistent across the performance. Soloists may overpower or get lost within the ensemble. Many passages achieve balance between soloists and ensemble, but recurring problems with blend among harmonized vocal parts or sensitivity between voices and live or recorded accompaniment interrupt otherwise effective moments.
levels.example: “Waving Through a Window” chorus sections bury the solo slightly in stronger ensemble vocals. Blend lacks clarity. At a passage where solo voices and harmonies overlap, there are effective stretches in which the lead line remains distinct while supporting parts blend rather than compete. However, one part dominates the texture or the accompanying sound masks the lead at several points. Because the problem recurs rather than appearing once, the relationship among the musical lines becomes unclear during parts of the sequence, even though the overall scene still communicates.

levels.label: Good+
levels.observable: Frequent issues with internal vocal balance or lead/ensemble coordination. Blend among harmonized parts is repeatedly uneven. Repeated attempts at balance between soloists and ensemble, together with blend among harmonized vocal parts, are evident, yet sensitivity between voices and live or recorded accompaniment succeeds only intermittently.
levels.example: In “Good for You,” one part regularly overshadows the others. Group dynamics are uneven, creating a sense of vocal competition. At a passage where solo voices and harmonies overlap, some passages succeed because the lead line remains distinct while supporting parts blend rather than compete. However, one part dominates the texture or the accompanying sound masks the lead in many of the more demanding moments. The intended effect is attempted throughout, but the relationship among the musical lines becomes unclear often enough that the result is only intermittently secure.

levels.label: Good
levels.observable: Disconnected ensemble; instrumental or vocal parts dominate instead of unify. Some passages demonstrate balance between soloists and ensemble; inconsistent blend among harmonized vocal parts and sensitivity between voices and live or recorded accompaniment prevent those successes from carrying through the performance.
levels.example: “You Will Be Found” feels vocally disorganized; leads are difficult to hear clearly above track or ensemble. At a passage where solo voices and harmonies overlap, a few isolated moments show that the lead line remains distinct while supporting parts blend rather than compete. Elsewhere, one part dominates the texture or the accompanying sound masks the lead frequently; as a result, the relationship among the musical lines becomes unclear and the dramatic intention comes through only in patches. The successes are real, but they do not yet form a dependable pattern.

levels.label: Developing
levels.observable: Balance problems distract from the overall vocal sound and storytelling. Occasional efforts at balance between soloists and ensemble are evident, but repeated problems with blend among harmonized vocal parts and sensitivity between voices and live or recorded accompaniment obscure most relevant moments.
levels.example: In “For Forever,” the lead is barely audible due to over-projected harmonies or an unbalanced mic mix. At a passage where solo voices and harmonies overlap, one brief passage suggests that the lead line remains distinct while supporting parts blend rather than compete. In most passages, however, one part dominates the texture or the accompanying sound masks the lead. Consequently, the relationship among the musical lines becomes unclear; the results are mixed and the dramatic intention is only occasionally recognizable.

levels.label: Fair+
levels.observable: Major blend issues undermine most group numbers. Only rare passages achieve balance between soloists and ensemble; persistent weaknesses in blend among harmonized vocal parts and sensitivity between voices and live or recorded accompaniment undermine the major moments.
levels.example: Ensemble voices clash in “Disappear.” Pitches may be correct, but volume inconsistencies weaken musical unity. At a passage where solo voices and harmonies overlap, only a few fragments suggest that the lead line remains distinct while supporting parts blend rather than compete. Much more often, one part dominates the texture or the accompanying sound masks the lead; the relationship among the musical lines becomes unclear across the number. The audience might recognize one successful beat but cannot rely on the criterion being achieved.

levels.label: Fair
levels.observable: Lack of blend makes music difficult to follow or enjoy. Convincing balance between soloists and ensemble is barely present, while substantial failures in blend among harmonized vocal parts and sensitivity between voices and live or recorded accompaniment dominate the performance.
levels.example: Voice parts are indistinguishable or dominate erratically. Track volume and soloist do not sync in emotional climaxes. At a passage where solo voices and harmonies overlap, a rare moment hints that the lead line remains distinct while supporting parts blend rather than compete, but one part dominates the texture or the accompanying sound masks the lead dominates almost every relevant passage. Consequently, the relationship among the musical lines becomes unclear to such an extent that the principal musical or dramatic information is obscured.

levels.label: Inadequate
levels.observable: No apparent blend or coordination between singers and musicians. Across relevant moments, balance between soloists and ensemble; blend among harmonized vocal parts; and sensitivity between voices and live or recorded accompaniment are virtually absent or ineffective.
levels.example: Group and solo vocals conflict or collapse entirely. Key moments in “You Will Be Found” are unintelligible due to unbalanced volume and unclear entrances. At a passage where solo voices and harmonies overlap, there is virtually no sustained moment in which the lead line remains distinct while supporting parts blend rather than compete. Instead, one part dominates the texture or the accompanying sound masks the lead throughout the sequence; the relationship among the musical lines becomes unclear so consistently that the intended contribution to the production is nearly absent.

criteria.title: STORY DEPICTION: Pacing, Transitions, and Energy
assessment_focus: Musical pacing, tempo, and energy aligned with dramatic stakes and story progression
Seamless movement between dialogue, songs, and musical sections
Songs treated as extensions of dialogue and character development
Rhythmic vitality, emotional connection, and sustained narrative momentum

levels.label: Superior
levels.observable: Musical pacing and transitions elevate narrative momentum. Energy levels shift appropriately and all transitions feel intentional and fluid. All relevant passages demonstrate tempo and dramatic pacing; transitions between speech, song, and musical sections; and musical energy serving the story’s emotional arc, without a consequential lapse.
levels.example: In Dear Evan Hansen, the shift from “You Will Be Found” into scene underscores is seamless, carrying emotional impact. Songs like “Waving Through a Window” grow in intensity without rushing tempo, showing dynamic control. At a transition from dialogue into a musical phrase, the pickup, tempo, and musical energy follow the character’s dramatic impulse. This clarity holds through exposed details as well as the busiest parts of the sequence; the audience receives the dramatic information without having to compensate for performance or design problems.

levels.label: Excellent+
levels.observable: Transitions and energy flow are effective with only brief moments of disconnection or push. Nearly every passage demonstrates tempo and dramatic pacing as well as transitions between speech, song, and musical sections; at most one isolated lapse in musical energy serving the story’s emotional arc is quickly resolved.
levels.example: Musical pacing in “For Forever” is emotionally timed, though transitions into “Sincerely, Me” feel slightly rushed or tonally abrupt. At a transition from dialogue into a musical phrase, the pickup, tempo, and musical energy follow the character’s dramatic impulse for nearly the entire sequence. On one brief occasion, the entrance feels detached from the spoken scene or the tempo works against the action; the issue is corrected immediately, so the intended storytelling remains clear. That isolated lapse distinguishes this from completely sustained excellence.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.observable: Overall flow supports storytelling, though some songs or transitions feel slightly forced or unbalanced. Most relevant passages demonstrate tempo and dramatic pacing; a few minor, separate lapses affect transitions between speech, song, and musical sections or musical energy serving the story’s emotional arc without forming a pattern.
levels.example: “Good for You” is energetic and emotionally clear, but its entrance after a dramatic scene feels too sudden or high-energy without buildup. At a transition from dialogue into a musical phrase, the pickup, tempo, and musical energy follow the character’s dramatic impulse in most moments. A few separate beats reveal that the entrance feels detached from the spoken scene or the tempo works against the action, but they are small and do not develop into a recurring weakness. The audience can still understand the scene’s central intention.

levels.label: Strong
levels.observable: Pacing choices vary across numbers. Some transitions feel disconnected or songs drag/rush. Many passages achieve tempo and dramatic pacing, but recurring problems with transitions between speech, song, and musical sections or musical energy serving the story’s emotional arc interrupt otherwise effective moments.
levels.example: “Requiem” lingers past its emotional peak, slowing scene progression. “Only Us” starts strong but rushes final measures. At a transition from dialogue into a musical phrase, there are effective stretches in which the pickup, tempo, and musical energy follow the character’s dramatic impulse. However, the entrance feels detached from the spoken scene or the tempo works against the action at several points. Because the problem recurs rather than appearing once, the story loses momentum at the very point music should advance it during parts of the sequence, even though the overall scene still communicates.

levels.label: Good+
levels.observable: Inconsistent flow disrupts the arc of the story. Transitions between songs/scenes are often jarring. Repeated attempts at tempo and dramatic pacing, together with transitions between speech, song, and musical sections, are evident, yet musical energy serving the story’s emotional arc succeeds only intermittently.
levels.example: “If I Could Tell Her” transitions too quickly into dialogue, and “Words Fail” does not build in tempo or energy as the character unravels. At a transition from dialogue into a musical phrase, some passages succeed because the pickup, tempo, and musical energy follow the character’s dramatic impulse. However, the entrance feels detached from the spoken scene or the tempo works against the action in many of the more demanding moments. The intended effect is attempted throughout, but the story loses momentum at the very point music should advance it often enough that the result is only intermittently secure.

levels.label: Good
levels.observable: Storytelling momentum is impaired by disjointed musical pacing. Some passages demonstrate tempo and dramatic pacing; inconsistent transitions between speech, song, and musical sections and musical energy serving the story’s emotional arc prevent those successes from carrying through the performance.
levels.example: “You Will Be Found” begins strong but ensemble entrance is delayed. Energy stalls during verse/chorus transitions. At a transition from dialogue into a musical phrase, a few isolated moments show that the pickup, tempo, and musical energy follow the character’s dramatic impulse. Elsewhere, the entrance feels detached from the spoken scene or the tempo works against the action frequently; as a result, the story loses momentum at the very point music should advance it and the dramatic intention comes through only in patches. The successes are real, but they do not yet form a dependable pattern.

levels.label: Developing
levels.observable: Musical storytelling is confused; changes in tempo or energy are erratic or unmotivated. Occasional efforts at tempo and dramatic pacing are evident, but repeated problems with transitions between speech, song, and musical sections and musical energy serving the story’s emotional arc obscure most relevant moments.
levels.example: “Sincerely, Me” feels too fast to allow for comedic timing, while “Requiem” suffers from unresolved tempo fluctuation between singers. At a transition from dialogue into a musical phrase, one brief passage suggests that the pickup, tempo, and musical energy follow the character’s dramatic impulse. In most passages, however, the entrance feels detached from the spoken scene or the tempo works against the action. Consequently, the story loses momentum at the very point music should advance it; the results are mixed and the dramatic intention is only occasionally recognizable.

levels.observable: Flow issues consistently affect dramatic clarity and momentum. Only rare passages achieve tempo and dramatic pacing; persistent weaknesses in transitions between speech, song, and musical sections and musical energy serving the story’s emotional arc undermine the major moments.
levels.example: “Words Fail” pacing does not allow emotional shifts to land. Transitions between songs feel abrupt and disrupt scene intention. At a transition from dialogue into a musical phrase, only a few fragments suggest that the pickup, tempo, and musical energy follow the character’s dramatic impulse. Much more often, the entrance feels detached from the spoken scene or the tempo works against the action; the story loses momentum at the very point music should advance it across the number. The audience might recognize one successful beat but cannot rely on the criterion being achieved.

Across relevant moments, tempo and dramatic pacing; transitions between speech, song, and musical sections; and musical energy serving the story’s emotional arc are virtually absent or ineffective.
levels.example: Scenes drag or rush unpredictably, emotional shifts are lost, and musical numbers feel isolated from character journey. At a transition from dialogue into a musical phrase, there is virtually no sustained moment in which the pickup, tempo, and musical energy follow the character’s dramatic impulse. Instead, the entrance feels detached from the spoken scene or the tempo works against the action throughout the sequence; the story loses momentum at the very point music should advance it so consistently that the intended contribution to the production is nearly absent.

criteria.title: MUSICIANSHIP AND TECHNICAL ACCURACY: Intonation, Rhythm, Ensemble Precision
assessment_focus: Accurate intonation, tuning, and rhythmic execution
Clean, coordinated entrances, cutoffs, and musical transitions
Cohesive ensemble precision and consistent technical control
Confident, clear execution appropriate to the score and musical style

levels.label: Superior
levels.observable: Pit musicians play with excellent intonation, rhythmic accuracy, and articulation. Ensemble is tightly synchronized. All relevant passages demonstrate intonation and rhythmic precision; coordinated entrances, articulation, and cutoffs; and ensemble cohesion across instrumental sections, without a consequential lapse.
levels.example: In West Side Story, "Prologue" and "Dance at the Gym" are rhythmically complex and demand tight brass, woodwind, and percussion ensemble playing. A 10-level performance handles syncopation, dynamics, and precision with clean cutoffs and crisp entrances.
